title: Join-pullback realization of a restricted simplex extension category
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, quasicategories and full subcategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and inner and left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $C,J$ be small ordinary categories, let $p:E\to N(C)$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, let $d\geq0$, and let $\tau:\Delta^d\to E$. Let $g:\Delta^d\star N(J)\to N(C)$ restrict to $p\tau$ on $\Delta^d$. Form $V=E\times_{N(C)}(\Delta^d\star N(J))$, let $U\subseteq V$ be the inverse image of the terminal factor $N(J)$, and let $\bar\tau:\Delta^d\to V$ be the lift with coordinates $(\tau,\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d})$. Define $E_{\tau/}$ in degree $k$ by extensions $\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to E$ of $\tau$, with operators restricting the last block, and similarly define $N(C)_{p\tau/}$ and $V_{\bar\tau/}$. The map $g$ defines $\beta:N(J)\to N(C)_{p\tau/}$ by restriction along $\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d}\star\sigma$ for each $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(J)$. Put $L=E_{\tau/}\times_{N(C)_{p\tau/}}N(J)$, with projection $\rho:L\to N(J)$.

Then $V$ is a quasicategory, $U$ is a full subcategory of $V$, and $\bar\tau$ is nondegenerate with no vertex in $U$, whether or not $\tau$ or $p\tau$ is degenerate. There is a natural isomorphism of simplicial sets $L\cong V_{\bar\tau/}\times_VU$, compatible with evaluation of the terminal block and with the projection to $N(J)$. Under this isomorphism terminal evaluation $L\to U$ is a left fibration, and $L$ is a quasicategory. Restriction to the last vertex of $\Delta^d$ induces an isomorphism $N(C)_{p\tau/}\cong N(C)_{p\tau(d)/}$, taking $\beta$ to the map induced by $g|_{\{d\}\star N(J)}$. These assertions include $J=\varnothing$.

proof.text: The join $\Delta^d\star N(J)$ is the nerve of the ordinary join category $[d]\star J$: its simplices are exactly an initial monotone string in $[d]$ followed by a string in $J$, with the same restriction operators. The nerve of an ordinary category fills every inner horn by composing the missing consecutive arrows. Hence the join is a quasicategory. Given an inner horn in $V$ and a prescribed simplex in the join over which it lies, lift the horn through the inner fibration $p$; this proves that $V$ is a quasicategory. The displayed map $\bar\tau$ is the pair $(\tau,\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d})$ by construction.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, pp. 340-341; join pullback setup

proof.text: A simplex of $V$ whose vertices all lie over the terminal factor $N(J)$ is, degreewise in the join decomposition, a simplex of the pure $N(J)$ summand; conversely every such simplex lies in the inverse image $U$. Thus $U$ is the full subcategory on those vertices. Every vertex of $\bar\tau$ lies in the initial $\Delta^d$ factor, so no vertex lies in $U$. If $\bar\tau$ were degenerate, its second coordinate $\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d}$ would be a nonidentity degeneracy of the identity simplex, which is impossible. Therefore $\bar\tau$ is nondegenerate even when $\tau$ or $p\tau$ is degenerate.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, p. 340; terminal-factor and lifted-simplex observations

proof.text: For each $k$, a $k$-simplex of $V_{\bar\tau/}\times_VU$ is a map $h:\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to V$ extending $\bar\tau$ whose last-block evaluation lies in $U$. Projecting to the join gives a map $\gamma:\Delta^d\star\Delta^k\to\Delta^d\star N(J)$ that is the identity on the first block and whose last block lands in $N(J)$. The degreewise join decomposition forces $\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d}\star\sigma$ for a unique $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(J)$. Projecting $h$ to $E$ then gives an extension of $\tau$ and the equality $ph=g\circ(\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^d}\star\sigma)$, hence a $k$-simplex of $L$. Conversely, a pair $(\sigma,h)$ in the definition of $L$ gives exactly such an $h$ and terminal evaluation in $U$. These mutually inverse correspondences commute with all restrictions, so they define a natural simplicial isomorphism $L\cong V_{\bar\tau/}\times_VU$, over $N(J)$ and over $U$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3 proof, p. 340; identification of the restricted join-pullback slice

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] with $\mathcal C=V$, $\mathcal D=\Delta^0$, $q:V\to\Delta^0$, $K=\Delta^d$, $K_0=\varnothing$, and $f=\bar\tau$. The map $q$ is an inner fibration because $V$ is a quasicategory by Step 1. Since $V_{f_0/}=V$ and both coslices of $\Delta^0$ are $\Delta^0$, the displayed target $\mathcal E$ in that lemma identifies with $V$, and its map $\rho$ is exactly terminal-block evaluation $V_{\bar\tau/}\to V$. Thus this projection is a left fibration. Pull it back along $U\hookrightarrow V$: a left-horn lifting square for the pullback gives one for the original map over the prescribed simplex in $U$, and pairing the lift with that simplex gives the required lift in the pullback. Also $U$ is a quasicategory: an inner horn in $U$ fills in $V$, and every vertex of the filler belongs to $U$, so fullness from Step 2 puts the filler in $U$. An inner horn in $V_{\bar\tau/}\times_VU$ can therefore be filled by first filling its projection in $U$ and then lifting that filler along the left fibration. Via the isomorphism of Step 3, terminal evaluation $L\to U$ is a left fibration and $L$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8, specialized to q:V -> Delta^0 and K_0 empty; equivalently Corollary 4.3.6.12 (018K) and Proposition 4.3.6.1 (018F). The pullback and full-subcategory horn arguments are written out here.

proof.text: An $k$-simplex of $N(C)_{p\tau/}$ is a functor $[d]\star[k]\to C$ extending the functor $[d]\to C$ represented by $p\tau$. Restriction to the last vertex of $[d]$ gives a functor $\{d\}\star[k]\to C$. In the inverse direction, compose every arrow from an earlier vertex $i\le d$ to the last vertex $d$ with the arrows in this restricted functor; the resulting composites are forced, and associativity gives the unique extension on all mixed simplices. These constructions are inverse in every degree and commute with simplicial operators, so restriction induces $N(C)_{p\tau/}\cong N(C)_{p\tau(d)/}$. Under this correspondence the map $\beta$ is carried to the map induced by $g|_{\{d\}\star N(J)}$, since both are obtained by restricting $g$ along the same last-vertex inclusion. The argument uses only ordinary nerve composition and includes $J=\varnothing$.
